text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Croatia become a part of the European road network. Transport Minister Zeljko Luzavec also signed a convention on river routes in Helsinki.
- The Hagueinternational war crimes tribunal discuss the status of witnesses ahead of the trial against Tihomir Blaskic.
- United States opens a commercial office in Zagreb.
- Croatia is developing pilotless aircraft for civilian and military use, says Ivan Carapina, member of the board of Koncar group's special equipment and systems unit.
- NATO will leave Bosnia in June 1998, according to U.S. deputy defence secretary John White.
- Croatia should present its tourist offer for 1998 soon but prices are difficult to determine due to uncertainty about VAT, to be introduced from January next year.
- Croatia has 500 smaller factory energy units which could be turned into modern power plants, providing cheaper energy.
- Banks are prepared to finance government purchases of the wheat crop, Agriculture Minister Zlatko Dominikovic tells wheat buyers.
- Indonesia is interested in new Croatian antibiotics and is offering joint-venture production in Indonesia to cut costs and facilitate the penetration of neighbouring markets.
- Taxpayers owe the inland revenue office 319.2 million kuna in 1996 income tax.

- The government and management of the state railways must take urgent steps to restructure the company. Labour cuts and abolishing some rail routes may be necessary to reduce its huge losses, according to a study made Canadian consultants CANAC.
- Tourism Minister Niko Bulic expects results of this year's tourist season to provide a basis to plans even more ambitious strategy in 1998. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 381-1-4557075
